- Overestimate prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values.
- Underestimate prices in the late part of the forecast horizon; adjust upward for persistent upward trends or mean reversion.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes; cap forecast values at 1–2% below the peak observed in the 30-day history.
- Model tends to overreact to recent volatility; dampen forecast sensitivity to short-term price swings.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is above 30-day moving average, reduce by 5–10% for the next 5–7 days.
- Lagged response: forecast often lags true price movements by 2–3 days; adjust for 1–2 day lead-in to recent price changes.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high prices; if last 5 days are above 75% of 30-day average, reduce forecast by 5–10%.
